alternatives_considered: A separate market for each reported NAPCS product was rejected: industry-product relationships establish reported products, not a shared operating identity.
Narrow prior candidate seeds were rejected because none is evidenced as equivalent to the integrated multi-function boundary.
The two specialist proposals were merged under the clearer integrated-outsourced-office-administration formulation.
analysis_summary: The evidence directly supports one operating market: contract- or fee-based delivery of an integrated range of day-to-day office administrative functions for client organizations. The defining boundary requires a range of functions and excludes complete operation of the client business; the manual also separates management consulting, property management, computer facilities management, construction management, food-service management, and single-support-service providers. NAPCS identities are reported product identities associated with the industry and are not themselves operating-market identities.

candidate_dispositions.rationale: A narrow dispatch/billing workflow does not evidence the required integrated range of office functions.

proposed_markets.acquisition_universe: Providers principally delivering an integrated range of outsourced day-to-day office administrative functions to client organizations.
proposed_markets.ambient_ai_workflow: AI may assist billing, recordkeeping, personnel administration, logistics coordination, and document workflows; no evidence supports an AI-specific market split.
proposed_markets.boundary: Contracted delivery across multiple day-to-day office functions, including financial planning, billing and recordkeeping, personnel, and physical-distribution/logistics administration. Excludes complete operation of the client business, management advice without day-to-day management, internally managed offices, property management, computer facilities management, construction management, food-service management, staffing, and standalone specialist support services.
proposed_markets.buyer: Organizations outsourcing a range of recurring office-administration responsibilities to an external provider.
proposed_markets.definition: Contracted provision of an integrated range of day-to-day office administrative services for other organizations, without providing operating staff to run the client's complete business.
proposed_markets.delivery_model: Contract- or fee-based recurring managed delivery across multiple administrative functions.
proposed_markets.economics_risk: Labor-enabled service economics depend on reliable execution, standardized processes, client scope, and accountability for recurring administrative workflows; the evidence does not support a narrower economic segmentation.
explicit_exclusions: Complete operation of a client's business with operating staff
Internal corporate, subsidiary, and regional managing offices
proposed_markets.job_to_be_done: Run a client's recurring office-administration functions as an integrated external service.
proposed_markets.workforce_model: Administrative personnel performing coordinated finance, billing, recordkeeping, personnel, and logistics tasks for client organizations.

adopted_elements: Exclusions for complete operation and standalone single-function services
NAPCS identities treated as non-market product identities
specialist_resolution.assessment: Both specialists converge on the same operating boundary. The adjudication retains the clearer integrated-outsourced-office-administration name and corrects the classification of NAPCS entries from no-family-mapping to non-market source identities.

adopted_elements: Explicit separation of consulting, property management, computer facilities management, construction management, and full business operation
specialist_resolution.assessment: The proposal is directly aligned with the NAICS definition and is adopted with slightly more explicit workforce and economics wording.
